In 44 ABY, Luke encountered Abeloth, who used Ming's appearance and Force-essence to make him believe that she was indeed his lost love. Fooled for only a minute, the realization of what had happened to Callista - and that he could not save her - caused Luke a great deal of pain as that, even after three decades, the love he had felt for her was still there. However, Luke was eventually able to sever Callista from Abeloth, allowing her to return to the light side.

===[[Akanah Norand Goss Pell]]===
Akanah entered Luke's life as he was meditating on his role in the Force. She told him that she knew of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Luke's mother]] and took him around the galaxy looking for her. They were initially just on friendly terms, until Akanah found out that her father was severely brain-damaged. At that point, Akanah and Luke grew close as Luke empathized and comforted her over her loss. However, this romance was also doomed to fail as Akanah had been deceiving him all along&mdash;she knew nothing of his mother. The relationship ended after that.

===[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]]===
[[File:Lukemarawedding.jpg|thumb|left|Skywalker and Mara Jade kiss in their apartment on Coruscant.]]
Mara Jade was a former Emperor's Hand whose last order had been to kill Luke. Their relationship was shaky at first, but they were forced to cooperate on numerous occasions to survive. As Mara worked with Luke, she developed at first a grudging respect for him, then later a growing admiration, tempered by her pragmatism and coolness as usual. While fighting on Nirauan, in order to coordinate their efforts perfectly, Luke and Mara performed a Force Meld, linking their minds. It was after understanding each other on so deep a level that they realized the depth of their attraction for each other. The two were falling in love and were happily married. Luke and Mara had a son that they named Ben, in honor of the memory of his first master, Obi-Wan 'Ben' Kenobi. Their marriage came to a tragic end when Mara was killed in a duel with Jacen Solo shortly before he became Darth Caedus. The pain Luke felt at the time of her death led him to kill Lumiya under the mistaken belief that it was she who killed Mara. He would meet Mara later after her death in the [[Lake of Apparitions]] only to be told that it wasn't her comforting him while he was asleep, and that it was [[Abeloth]].

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Anakin wasn't what he was supposed to become. But the son could become that.|George Lucas|<ref name="RS" />}}
Luke Skywalker appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]; the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novel]] depicted him slightly before the film's release in [[1977]]. He would go on to be born in the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|conclusion]] of the [[prequel trilogy]], in [[2005]]. However, that his sister, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]], and he would be born in the prequels was announced in [[1998]]. The [[original trilogy]] was [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|rereleased in theaters and VHS]] to commemorate the twenty year anniversary of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] [[1997|the year before]] and [[Star Wars Trivial Pursuit]] was released to coincide with this. The limited edition game, released in 1998, contained a sequestered pack of questions that served as a preview of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|the first new trilogy installment]], one of which divulged this. Back in 2005, [[George Lucas]] stated in an interview with [https://www.rollingstone.com Rolling Stone], that [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]] wanted Luke Skywalker because he could become what his father couldn't: "''somebody who would be more powerful than he was and could help him rule the universe''" ―George Lucas<ref name="RS">{{WebCite|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-news/george-lucas-and-the-cult-of-darth-vader-247142|text=George Lucas and the Cult of Darth Vader|date=2005-06-02|author=Gavin Edwards|archivedate=20220610171111}}</ref> due to the events that occurred on [[Mustafar]], presented in '''[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]'''.

===Origins of Luke===
The name "Luke" is likely derived from [[George Lucas]]'s own name. One reason Lucas may have done this is to reflect his own identification with the character.

The name Luke is derived from the name of a region in [[Wikipedia:Italy|Italy]], [[Wikipedia:Lucania|Lucania]], through the Greek "Loukas," meaning "a native of Lucania." It is most famous as the name of a Christian Evangelist, the author of the [[Wikipedia:Gospel of Luke|Gospel of Luke]].<ref name="etym">{{WebCite|url=https://www.etymonline.com/word/Luke|text=Etymology Online|archiveurl=https://archive.is/rCipJ}}</ref>

[[File:MCQ-deakvader.jpg|thumb|right|340px|Early concept art showing Deak Starkiller fighting Darth Vader]]
In the biography of George Lucas on The Academy of Achievement website, it is noted that the famous [[Skywalker Ranch]] is, in fact, named after Luke Skywalker.<ref name="Academy of Achievement">{{WebCite|url=https://www.achievement.org/autodoc/page/luc0int-1|text=George Lucas Interview &mdash; Academy of Achievement|archivedate=20161128193336}}</ref>

In early drafts of the ''A New Hope'' screenplay, the main character who became Luke was a girl named Starkiller. In other drafts, Luke was an experienced sixty-five year old [[General/Legends|General]] rather than a youth. Just before the final script was written, his surname was Starkiller, when later it was changed to Skywalker.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|lukeskywalker|Skywalker, Luke}}</ref> In the scene where Luke first meets Leia on the Death Star, he introduces himself as Luke Starkiller; this was later reshot after the executives at 20th Century Fox expressed their displeasure at the name.<ref>Interview with [[Mark Hamill]] on "Where Are They Now?" 10/6/07</ref> The Starkiller name later was used for a Tarisian duel veteran in the times of [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], named [[Gorse Bendak|Bendak Starkiller]],<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> and even more recently as the name of Darth Vader's secret apprentice, [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]].<ref name="Starkiller">{{WebCite|url=http://www.nzgamer.com/ps3/news/2563/exclusive-the-force-unleashed-information.html|text=NZGamer.com &ndash; Exclusive The Force Unleashed Information!|archivedate=20081025110442}}</ref> Starkiller being Luke's pre-production name, however, was referenced in the ''Fate of the Jedi'' series novel ''Outcast'', where Luke, when expressing reluctance to utilize an ability Jacen mastered out of fear of it causing his transformation into a Sith, sarcastically refers to himself as "Darth Starkiller" upon explaining this to Ben.

George Lucas has stated that Luke has the same Force potential as his father, which is why both Darth Vader and the Emperor were willing to turn on each other to gain Luke as their apprentice. Luke is said to represent Anakin's full potential, if Anakin had lived to achieve it rather than suffer the horrible fate that made him more machine than man. Lucas also mentions that Luke's Force potential was even more powerful than Emperor Palpatine's.<ref name="ESBDC" />

===Casting===
[[File:Hamill-Lucas.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Mark Hamill (right) and George Lucas (left) celebrating the 30th anniversary of ''Star Wars'' in 2007.]]
Luke Skywalker was portrayed by [[Mark Hamill]] and stuntman [[Colin Skeaping]] in the [[original trilogy]] and ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', and [[Aidan Barton]] (the son of editor [[Roger Barton]]) as an infant in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Hamill returned to provide the voice of Luke in the radio dramatizations of ''A New Hope'' and ''The Empire Strikes Back''. Hamill also played Luke in a number of comedy skits on TV. In [[1977]], he briefly played Luke on that year's edition of [[Wikipedia:Bob Hope|''The Bob Hope Christmas Special'']]. He played a primary role as Luke (and as himself&mdash;"Luke's cousin") on an episode of ''[[The Muppet Show]]'' in [[1980]].

Although Hamill continued on a career of voicing, Luke was portrayed by [[Bob Bergen]] in video and computer games, [[Joshua Fardon]] in the [[Return of the Jedi (radio)|''Return of the Jedi'' radio play]], and [[Mark Benninghofen]] in the audio adaptations of [[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Rebel Agent'']] and [[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight (audio drama)|''Jedi Knight'']] from the [[Star Wars: Dark Forces (novellas)|''Dark Forces'' novellas]]. In [[2000]], Mark Hamill reprised his role as Luke Skywalker for a speaking role in a [[Vector Prime television commercial|commercial]] for ''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]'', the first of the [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''New Jedi Order'']] novels by famous author [[R. A. Salvatore]]. In the commercial, he briefly recalls his past experiences as a Jedi and with the Rebel Alliance, and told of some new threat that he was unsure he could defeat. This threat would be revealed in the book as an [[Wikipedia:Alien (biology)|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from another galaxy known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]].<ref name="Vector Prime ad" /> Hamill's likeness was later used to portray older versions of Luke Skywalker in later novels, comics, and reference guides. In recent years, Hamill has also "reprised" his role by voicing both Luke and himself on shows such as [[Wikipedia:Family Guy|''Family Guy'']], [[Wikipedia:The Simpsons|''The Simpsons'']], and [[Wikipedia:Robot Chicken|''Robot Chicken'']].

[[Ben Burtt]], the sound designer and main editor of the ''Star Wars'' films, also auditioned for the character's role.

Luke Skywalker has also been portrayed in voice-overs by [[C. Andrew Nelson]] in [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']], [[Lloyd Floyd]] in various recent video games and the Lego short [[LEGO Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Out|''The Empire Strikes Out'']], and [[Matt Lanter]] in the radio drama ''[[Star Wars: Smuggler's Gambit]]''.

===Non-canon storylines===
====''The Force Unleashed'' series====
{{Quote|I won't run from my destiny, or from you.|Luke Skywalker, to Lord Starkiller|<ref name="TFU:USE">{{TFU|USE=1}}</ref>}}
[[File:Stalker_vs_Skywalker.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Skywalker clashes with Galen Marek as Palpatine's servant in the non-canon "Ultimate Sith" edition of ''The Force Unleashed'']]
In addition to all the stories about Luke in the ''Star Wars'' [[Canon|continuity]], there are also certain non-canon publications. ''Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back'' and ''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition'' both present non-canon versions of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the former involves Luke's [[Death/Legends|death]] and the latter involves his fall to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]].

In ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]'', another Infinity follows [[Galen Marek|Lord Starkiller]], who became the Emperor's new apprentice after destroying Darth Vader, as he infiltrates Echo Base. The opening crawl reveals that Luke has been trained in the Force by Obi-Wan Kenobi's spirit, yet Luke was still under the impression that his father had been betrayed and murdered by Vader until Starkiller goads Luke with the truth. The Emperor sends orders via Starkiller's liaison that Luke should be taken alive, implicitly so that the Emperor may replace Starkiller with an unbroken apprentice.

Like in the mainstream continuity, Luke tries to stand between his friends and the Sith. This becomes Luke's undoing; while he and Starkiller duel in the Echo Base hangar, the latter uses the Force to prevent the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} escape. Luke secures his friends' release, but at the cost of turning to the dark side of the Force and becoming Starkiller's apprentice.

Prior to the events in the Endor DLC of ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'', Leia Organa explains to the [[Dark Apprentice]] that Luke Skywalker fell on Hoth. Due to her twin brother's untimely demise, Leia was forced to take up Luke's destiny by training as a Jedi. Although her skills were impressive to the dark clone, she would ultimately share in her brother's fate after being outmatched and overpowered by her father's Sith assassin.

====Comics====
{{Quote|I told you I'd keep him safe, and I will. Even if that means from you.|Owen to Obi-Wan, discussing Luke after Maul's attack|<ref name="Old Wounds">{{StoryCite|story=Old Wounds|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>}}
In ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', Han fails to find Luke in time, and he freezes to death on Hoth after escaping from the [[Wampa/Legends|wampa's]] cave. Instead, Leia trains to become a Jedi.

[[File:Toddler_Luke.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Three-year old Luke Skywalker as depicted in "Old Wounds."]]
In the [[2005]]<ref name="Old Wounds" /> non-canon<ref name="SWBoards">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=125719&start=0675#10095628|thread=Event Timeline and Character Age Discussion|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2005-03-29|time=11:02 AM}}</ref> comic "[[Old Wounds]]," written and illustrated by [[Aaron McBride]] and published in the anthology ''[[Star Wars: Visionaries]]'', Luke appears as a youngling.<ref name="Old Wounds" /> In [[16 BBY/Legends|16 BBY]],<ref name="Old Wounds Date">The opening panel of "[[Old Wounds]]" places the events of the comic in the third [[Standard year/Legends|year]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] occupation of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], which took place in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Therefore, "Old Wounds" must be set in [[16 BBY/Legends|16 BBY]].</ref> Skywalker and his uncle were watching the sunset at their farm while Owen taught Luke to say the word "vaporators." Owen told Luke that the twin suns of Tatooine needed to rest and observed that Luke was growing weary as well. The farmer then heard something in the distance and saw a figure approaching: the Sith Lord [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], who had survived his apparent death [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|on Naboo]] and sought revenge on Kenobi for bisecting him. Owen called Beru to bring him his [[GRS-1 snare rifle/Legends|rifle]] and to take Luke inside. As Maul reached Owen, the Sith knocked him down and approached Beru and Luke, with the aunt begging him not to hurt them.<ref name="Old Wounds" />

Maul expressed recognition of Luke as Vader's son before sensing Kenobi's presence. The Sith then recounted his journey to find Kenobi&mdash;which included finding medical records on Polis Massa&mdash;explaining that he knew by finding Luke that he could draw Kenobi out. The Jedi Master then burst out from underground and engaged Maul in a [[Duel at the Lars homestead|duel]]. While they fought, Beru, still carrying Luke, crawled over to Owen to check on him. Eventually, Kenobi had his lightsaber deactivated and held against Maul's head, but was unable to deliver the killing blow. Owen grabbed his rifle and shot Maul himself. Afterward, Kenobi asked if Luke was alright, to which Owen responded that he had promised to keep Luke safe, even if it meant from Kenobi, and that the Jedi was forbidden to return to the farm. As Kenobi carried Maul's body out to the Dune Sea to burn it, he telepathically communicated with Luke, vowing that he would always be present even if Luke could not see him.<ref name="Old Wounds" />

====LEGO====
Luke's adventures from the original trilogy are humorously retold in ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' and ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''. While these games follow the mainstream continuity, the manner in which the events are presented and the various plot elements added for gameplay or fun make the game non-canon.

===Translations===
In the French [[original trilogy]], Luke is called "'''Luc'''".
